ratings.reviewer_notes: [AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] The study directly investigates the cellular mechanisms of anti-PD-1 therapy-induced lung toxicity, identifying ICOS+CD4 T cells in an aged environment as a key driver.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] This is a review article providing context on the immunological changes and cytokine dysregulation (e.g., IFNgamma, TNF, CD8+ T-cell dominance) associated with checkpoint inhibitor-induced irAEs.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] This review provides useful context on the mechanisms of cardiovascular toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, including T cell activation and inflammatory cytokines.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] The study directly addresses the mechanism of PD-1 inhibitor-related cardiotoxicity, linking it to a reduction in intracardiac regulatory T cells and alterations in gut microbiota.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] This review discusses preclinical models of ICI-mediated cardiotoxicity, highlighting the roles of CD8+ T cells, cytokines, and macrophages, providing review-level context.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] A review article summarizing the pathogenic mechanisms of ICI-associated cardiovascular toxicity, such as T cell activation and cytokine release storms.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] This meta-analysis evaluates the association between the occurrence of irAEs and clinical efficacy/survival, but does not investigate the biological mechanisms linking PD-1 blockade to irAEs.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] The study directly tests the mechanism by which anti-PD-1 treatment exacerbates autoimmunity (EAE model), showing it augments pathogenic IL-17A-producing gammadelta T cells.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] Uses a genetic knockout model (loss of Ctla4 and Pdcd1) rather than pharmacological blockade to study ICI-associated myocarditis, providing a different but highly informative model of the mechanism.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] The study directly investigates the mechanism of anti-PD-1-induced myocarditis, demonstrating the contribution of cardiac myosin-specific autoimmune T cells.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] Directly addresses the mechanism of CPI-induced colitis (including anti-PD-1), showing dependence on the intestinal microbiota and an IL23/IFNgamma axis.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] A review article that bridges the gap between PD-1 signaling, ICI-induced irAEs, and primary autoimmune diseases, providing useful review-level context.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] Directly investigates the mechanism of ICI-induced myocarditis, establishing that PD-1 blockade permits priming of autoreactive CD8 T cells and that injury depends on T cell-derived TNF.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] A review of skin manifestations induced by ICIs that briefly outlines the underlying mechanisms, providing review-level context.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] Directly addresses the mechanism of toxicity in dual CTLA-4 and PD-1 immunotherapy, identifying TNF upregulation as a key driver of colitis.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] The article focuses on the clinical presentation and management of hematologic irAEs rather than investigating the underlying biological mechanisms linking PD-1 blockade to these events.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] Directly investigates the immune signatures and mechanisms of checkpoint inhibitor-induced neurotoxicity, identifying specific T cell and B cell dysregulation.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] Studies a patient with inherited PD-1 deficiency, providing a different but highly informative genetic model for understanding the mechanisms of autoimmunity related to PD-1 loss of function.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] Directly links the occurrence of anti-PD-1 irAEs to a specific mechanism/correlate: high therapeutic antibody occupancy of PD-1 receptors on CD4+ T cells.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] A case series that provides adjacent evidence implicating the IL-23/IL-17 axis in the mechanism of psoriatic arthritis flares during ICI therapy.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] A review article summarizing the possible mechanisms of various immune-related adverse events caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors.

[AI-GENERATED RATING -- Gemini 3.1 Pro. Supplementary multi-model cross-check.] This preclinical characterization of nivolumab notes a lack of adverse immune-related events in macaques, thus providing no usable evidence on the mechanisms linking PD-1 blockade to irAEs.
